correctness.rationale: The source quartic is explicitly parametrized by additive polynomials with inverse \(w^8=z+y^2\). Its direction map has a separable cubic numerator equation; symmetric resolvent identities yield \(R^2+R=1+B^3/A\) and a rigorously smooth elliptic Weierstrass model when \(1+\alpha^3\ne0\). Counting cubic Frobenius types including the two exceptional slopes yields \(\#E=6+6s_4\). The \(t^3=1\) case is separately proved using quadratic trace. All 246 parameter instances over GF(4) through GF(128) passed exhaustive exact point/direction/cubic tests. Universal quantification rests on algebra, not tests.

originality.rationale: Section 3 of Hilario–Stöhr (arXiv:2211.16962) supplies the pencil and its geometric singularity/tangency facts; the two follow-up papers describe general forms and tangent geometry. None of the inspected relevant sections states or logically yields the exact 0/1/2/4 rational-line spectrum or its genus-one Frobenius controlling identity without an additional cubic-direction/resolvent computation. Classical quadratic resolvent and Artin–Schreier theory are accepted as prior tools. A specific unindexed-papers risk remains.
residual_risks: The full unindexed characteristic-two linear-set and cubic-Galois-cover literature was not exhaustively surveyed.
The article versions inspected need not match every subsequent journal addendum; no independent specialist priority check was performed.

value.rationale: The rational-line intersection spectrum is a natural enumerative invariant of a characteristic-two projective plane curve that the motivating geometric classification leaves undetermined. The nontrivial arithmetic jump varies with the elliptic Frobenius trace, and the exceptional \(t^3=1\) degeneration is classified exactly. The result gives a uniform complete classification for all eligible fields and parameters, not an arbitrary finite table or a textbook exercise.
